source_name: Eurostat ICT usage in households and by individuals (isoc_i) — Montenegro national metadata + databrowser
why_relevant: The isoc_i family is the EU-harmonised source for internet-banking usage, e-commerce and online-payment behaviour. Montenegro has run the survey since 2011 and transmits microdata to Eurostat, so ME appears alongside EU averages — the best comparable demand-side digital-payments proxy between Findex waves. The '_me' country-specific metadata file confirms ME reporting.

source_name: ECB — Western Balkans / candidate-country central banking cooperation and euroisation research
why_relevant: The ECB runs an EU-funded technical cooperation programme with the Central Bank of Montenegro on ESCB-standard alignment (including statistics), and publishes Occasional Papers assessing financial stability and euroisation in candidate countries. Montenegro is unilaterally euroised, which shapes cash-usage dynamics; note the ECB explicitly does NOT collect euro-substitution data for countries where the euro is legal tender (Montenegro, Kosovo).

source_name: BIS CPMI — payments and FMI statistics ('Red Book') and country payment-system information
why_relevant: The definitional and methodological benchmark for payment statistics (cards, e-money, terminals, transaction values) even though Montenegro is NOT a CPMI member and is therefore outside the Red Book country set. Useful for aligning ME national series to internationally comparable definitions and as a comparator set for regional benchmarking.

source_name: DBnomics — IMF/FAS and other international series mirror
why_relevant: Independent open aggregator that mirrors IMF FAS (and IFS, Eurostat, World Bank) series with a stable free API and long history. Practical redundancy when official portals are re-platformed or rate-limited; useful for automated Montenegro time-series retrieval.

source_name: FRED (St. Louis Fed) — Montenegro international-source series mirror
why_relevant: Mirrors IMF FAS and World Bank GFDD indicators for Montenegro (e.g. ATM counts, remittance-to-GDP series such as DDOI11MEA156NWDB) with a clean API and vintage tracking, which is handy for detecting silent revisions in the upstream international series.

source_name: Central Bank of Montenegro — international institutions pages (IMF / World Bank counterpart view)
source_subtype: national central-bank page on international bodies
why_relevant: Local-language mirror of the supranational relationship: describes Montenegro's membership in the IBRD/IDA/IFC/MIGA group and IMF, and often links or references the data CBCG reports upward (FAS, FSI). Useful for reconciling nationally published figures with the international vintages and for local terminology.

source_name: UBCG — Članice udruženja (member bank list)
why_relevant: Enumerates all 11 licensed banks with their own websites (Addiko, Adriatic, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, NLB, Lovćen, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Zapad banka, Ziraat) — the seed list for bank-level disclosure cells (card portfolios, ATM/POS networks, fee tariffs).

source_name: Časopis "Bankar" — UBCG professional quarterly (issue archive)
why_relevant: The association's own peer/practitioner magazine, published since 2008 (issue 72 in Feb 2026), regularly carries sector analyses, payment-system and card/digital-banking articles authored by bank and CBCG staff — often with figures not repeated elsewhere. Full back-issues are downloadable PDFs under wp-content/uploads.

source_name: UBCG — Pregled rada za 2024. godinu (annual activity report)
why_relevant: Annual self-report of association activity: committee work (payment systems, cards, SEPA, security), projects, and sector positions. Useful for tracking which payment/card topics the industry is actively working on and who represents whom.

source_name: UBCG — Statut 2025 (association statute)
why_relevant: The 2025/2026 statute defines 11 expert committees with mandates, annual work plans and reporting duties — i.e. it tells you what documents the association is obliged to generate and therefore what can be requested or expected to appear.

source_name: UBCG — Novosti / Najave / Seminari (news, announcements, workshops)
why_relevant: Running record of association events that carry payment-market content: e.g. workshops on instant payments (Montran, QR-code solutions, Jan 2026), EU payment regulation (IPR, PSD3, FIDA, Feb 2026), AI-in-banking panel (Dec 2025), instant-payments readiness posts since 2021. Highest-frequency signal in this cell.

source_name: UBCG — SEPA section
why_relevant: Dedicated association page on SEPA migration — the single largest structural change to Montenegrin payment traffic; likely to carry timelines, scheme adherence status and bank readiness statements.

source_name: UBCG — Edukacija: Prevarne radnje (card/payment fraud education)
why_relevant: Output of the association's Commission for Prevention of Payment Card Misuse; fraud-awareness material occasionally carries incidence figures and channel breakdowns (card-not-present, ATM skimming) that are unavailable in official statistics.

source_name: UBCG — Propisi (regulations collection)
why_relevant: Association-curated set of banking/payment regulations; a shortcut map to which laws and CBCG decisions the industry considers binding on payment services, and a pointer into the legal-source cells.

source_name: European Banking Federation — Montenegro country page & "Facts & Figures"
why_relevant: UBCG is an associate EBF member; EBF publishes an annual Montenegro banking-sector Facts & Figures PDF (latest noted December 2024) compiled from association/national input, with an archive of previous editions — an English-language, comparable-format aggregate of the sector.

source_name: Interbalkan Forum of Banking Associations (IFBA)
why_relevant: UBCG is a full member; the forum's meetings gather regional banking associations and produce country presentations that often include payment/card sector snapshots, and it points to peer associations for cross-country benchmarking.

source_name: ATTF Luxembourg — training partner of UBCG
why_relevant: Long-standing technical-assistance partner delivering seminars to Montenegrin banks; seminar programmes reveal which payment/card capability gaps the sector is addressing.

source_name: INFINTECH conference (Porto Montenegro, Tivat) — organiser Logate, partner Mastercard
why_relevant: The main annual banking/fintech gathering for Montenegro and the wider SEE region; nine-panel programme covering instant payments, digital onboarding, cyber security and AI in banking. Agendas, speaker lists and post-event coverage routinely carry card/payment volume figures presented by banks and Mastercard.

source_name: MINA news agency — banking/association coverage
why_relevant: National news agency that carries UBCG institutional news verbatim (e.g. adoption of the new statute and 2026-2031 financial framework, annual banking/fintech event announcements) — useful for dating association developments and catching items not posted on ubcg.info.

source_name: CBCG press releases naming UBCG (joint statements, meetings)
why_relevant: Joint CBCG–commercial banks–Deposit Protection Fund–UBCG statements and meeting readouts are where sector-level positions (fees, payment-system changes, cash handling) get formalised; they cross-validate association claims against the regulator.

source_name: CompanyWall Montenegro — UBCG legal-entity record
why_relevant: Registry-derived profile of the association as a legal entity (NGO registered 7 April 2003, Novaka Miloševa bb, Podgorica), giving founding date, identifiers and possibly filed financials — useful for provenance and for locating the association's registered filings.

source_name: UBCG Facebook/social presence via bankar.me page (event and statement mirror)
why_relevant: Association assembly sessions and member-bank gatherings are announced/photographed on sector social pages before the website is updated; useful low-latency signal on committee activity and event occurrence.

source_name: Crnogorska komercijalna banka (CKB, OTP Group) — Za investitore / Finansijski izvještaji
why_relevant: Largest bank in Montenegro (26 branches, ~115 ATMs, claims >4,000 POS terminals). Its audited annual reports and management reports are the only entity-level disclosure of card issuance, ATM/POS estate and digital-channel users for the market leader.
